description: Mirror and Water Images are important concepts in the non-verbal section of Logical Reasoning. It involves identifying the inverted or reflected form of a given figure, letter, or number.

sections.title: Basic Concept of Mirror Image
sections.description: When an object is placed in front of a vertical mirror, the image formed is called a mirror image.

key_concepts.explanation: In a mirror image, the left side of the object appears on the right side, and the right side appears on the left side.
The top and bottom parts of the object remain completely unchanged in a mirror image.

sections.title: Basic Concept of Water Image
sections.description: When an object is placed above a water surface or a horizontal mirror, the image formed is called a water image.

key_concepts.explanation: In a water image, the top part of the object appears at the bottom, and the bottom part appears at the top.
The left and right parts of the object remain completely unchanged in a water image.

sections.title: Images of Letters and Numbers
sections.description: The mirror and water images of the English Alphabet and numbers have specific symmetries that are essential to memorize for quick problem-solving.

results: 11 capital letters remain unchanged in a mirror: A, H, I, M, O, T, U, V, W, X, Y.
8 capital letters remain unchanged in a water image: C, D, E, H, I, K, O, X.
4 letters look identical in both mirror and water images: H, I, O, X.

sections.title: Clock Based Images
sections.description: Specific mathematical formulas are used to find the exact mirror or water image of a given time on a clock without drawing.

equations: 11:60 - Given time (If the time is between 1 and 11 o'clock)
23:60 - Given time (If the time is between 11 and 1 o'clock)
18:30 - Given time (If minutes are 30 or less)
17:90 - Given time (If minutes are more than 30)

sections.title: Steps to Solve Figure Based Problems
sections.description: A systematic approach to solving complex problems involving non-verbal figures quickly and accurately.

steps.title: Rule of Proximity
steps.detail: Always remember that the part of the real figure closest to the mirror will also be the closest to the mirror in the reflected image.

steps.title: Elimination Method
steps.detail: Quickly eliminate options that violate basic rules (e.g., if the top and bottom change in a mirror image option, discard it immediately).

steps.title: Focus on Asymmetrical Elements
steps.detail: Instead of looking at the whole complex figure, focus on a specific point, arrow, or shaded region inside the figure and track its specific inversion.
